method: Ranked by claude-sonnet-5-5, which read 14 of 14 shortlisted pieces

picks.title: The energy of thought
picks.author: David Colaço & Philipp Haueis
picks.why_it_matters: Argues that mind models ignore metabolism. Brain energy budgets (about 20 W, roughly 500,000 ATP per synaptic bit) limit which theories of memory are viable.

picks.title: Michael Taylor on Combined Arms Operations, a Transhistorical Primer
picks.source: A Collection of Unmitigated Pedantry (Bret Devereaux)
picks.author: Bret Devereaux
picks.why_it_matters: Explains why combined arms is hard, from the Iron Age to today: incompatible combat mechanics, leadership blind spots, status, logistics and cost.

picks.title: Formlabs Form Studio 1 Teardown
picks.author: bunnie
picks.why_it_matters: Teardown that explains cost-down design: a single cast reference plate cancels tolerance stack-up, and assembly yield falls steeply with step count.

picks.title: Human military relevance is more important than economic relevance
picks.author: cousin_it
picks.why_it_matters: Argues masses gained power when firearms made them useful soldiers, not because they were productive, so AI soldiers would end that leverage.

picks.title: The Bombmaker Next Door
picks.author: Brendan Fitzgerald
picks.why_it_matters: Long reported story on clearing a dead suburban man's home of 400-plus explosives and booby traps, and the neighbors who never suspected.
